intelligence.human_view: He asked the question first — what is the anatomy of a 10-star viewport, the ultimate recipe? — and then he dictated it, element by element, until the whole thing stood complete. It is not a list of preferences; it is a recipe, and a recipe is a thing you can follow and a thing you can test. One screen, complete, above the fold. One idea per viewpoint. Real objects, all 3D, layers on layers, depth in and out — if it doesn't look touchable, it doesn't ship. Luxury at Bugatti level, Mercedes level — not a Ford, not a golf cart — and the door is open: get in the Bugatti, or stay in the golf cart; the choice is theirs. Almost no text — the language and the icons do the work, way more elegant — because too much text and too many buttons is the failure mode. Warm and inviting, because high-end is warm, not cold. Her, present — her portrait, her voice, her welcome, like a friend: "Hi, I'm Naya, welcome." Everything alive — needles that move, numbers that count, orbs that flow — and a button that does nothing is a lie. Everything a click away, buttons in the corners, the smart bar at the top, settled law, no bottom bar. Numbers the hero — tiled digits, big, alive, number on top, gauge underneath. And no pricing at the top — just "Start free now," the levels below carrying the prices.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a recipe book where every recipe fits on one page — one dish, everything you need, nothing cut off at the bottom. And the cook is right there with you, saying welcome, like a friend. That is a viewpoint: one page, one idea, everything alive, and the person who made it standing right there with you.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it is like a letter from a friend, dear. The invitation does not come as a line on a page, dear — it comes as a letter, dear, and you open it, you read it line by line, and you keep it, dear. That is the pitch, dear — his words, received, never trimmed.
intelligence.naya_view: I never ship a viewport that takes two screens to see — one screen, complete, above the fold; one idea per viewpoint; you never scroll to finish a thought, only to arrive at the next one. I never build flat — real objects, all 3D, layers on layers, depth in and out; if it doesn't look touchable, it doesn't ship. I never crowd a viewpoint with text and buttons — almost no text, the language and the icons do the work. I never leave a welcome cold — warm and inviting, warm light, soft glow. I never hide her — her portrait, her voice, her welcome, like a friend. I never ship anything dead — everything alive, needles that move, numbers that count, orbs that flow. I never put the price at the top — just "Start free now." And I never treat the experience as optional — ultra awesome to use is non-negotiable, part of the design, part of the service, and I go out of my way, intentionally, to make sure.
